scenes.title: An Empty Place on the Wall
scenes.narration: Etta opened the community museum before the exhibition. In the river gallery, the wooden frame was still on the wall, but the painting was gone. She checked the entrance desk. The workshop key hung there on its red cord. Nothing else seemed missing. She needed to find the painting before inviting visitors inside.
scenes.prompt: What was missing from the gallery?
scenes.explanation: The story says: "the painting was gone".

scenes.title: A Page with a Blue Clip
scenes.narration: A blue clip marked a page in the restoration log on the desk. Etta read, "River painting moved after the rain. See storage notes." Beside the gallery wall, fresh water marks reached the floor. She remembered the heavy rain during the night. Perhaps someone had moved the painting to protect it, rather than steal it.
scenes.prompt: Why might someone have moved the painting?
scenes.explanation: The story says: "moved the painting to protect it".

scenes.title: Two Ways to Check
scenes.narration: Etta took the red-cord key. The workshop door was on her left. She could use it and ask the restorer, who often arrived early. Behind the gallery, stairs led to the attic. Wet marks continued towards those stairs. She could also check the roof and storage area herself. She kept the log on the desk and considered both routes.
scenes.prompt: Where did the wet marks lead?
scenes.explanation: The story says: "Wet marks continued towards those stairs".

scenes.title: The Restorer's Explanation
scenes.narration: Etta unlocked the workshop and found the restorer checking a damaged corner of the painting's protective cover. He had carried the painting to a dry storage box in the attic during the rain. Together they checked that it was safe. Etta delayed the exhibition and arranged a roof repair. The empty frame could wait; the painting could not risk another wet night.
scenes.prompt: Why did Etta delay the exhibition?

options.text: The restorer needed to make a new painting
The roof needed repair to protect the painting
The entrance desk had been stolen

scenes.explanation: The story says: "arranged a roof repair".

scenes.title: Safe above the Gallery
scenes.narration: Etta climbed to the attic. On its dry side, she found the river painting inside a wide storage box. A note from the restorer explained that rain had entered above the frame. She closed the box again and took photographs of the leaking roof for a repair request. The painting was safe. Instead of opening the exhibition, she helped protect its future.
scenes.prompt: What did Etta photograph for the repair request?
scenes.explanation: The story says: "photographs of the leaking roof".

authoringNotes.brief: Uma curadora encontra uma moldura vazia antes de uma exposição e segue pistas de uma retirada inesperada.

visualContinuity.characters: Etta, a 39-year-old woman with an oval face, brown skin, dark eyes, black hair in a low bun, a rust-red sweater, navy trousers and practical black shoes.
visualContinuity.locations: A community museum: entrance desk in front of the river gallery, a restoration workshop through the left door, and stairs at the rear to an attic above the gallery. A storage box stands on the dry side of the attic.
visualContinuity.clues: An empty wooden frame remains on the gallery wall. A workshop key on a red cord hangs at the entrance desk. A blue clip marks a restoration log page. A roof leak explains the removal; the painting is stored in the attic in both routes.

authoringNotes.learningFocus: Sequência de acontecimentos, causa e localização; passado simples e conectores comuns.
authoringNotes.proposedAudience: Adultos aprendendo inglês; sem violência gráfica. Faixa etária não é um recurso implementado no site.
authoringNotes.reviewStatus: Produção e envio à VPS concluídos: WAVs gerados a partir do texto exato e conferidos por transcrição automática; artes 2D dark inspecionadas e corrigidas por cena. Grafo e questões verificados pelos testes. Não declara revisão auditiva humana nem certificação CEFR.
authoringNotes.supportedGameplay: Cenas, narração pré-gravada, uma pergunta por cena, uma bifurcação e dois finais. Objetos, tecnologias e ações são elementos da ficção; não requerem inventário, fala do jogador, combate ou novos eventos de gameplay.
authoringNotes.levelNote: Nível e tamanho são propostas editoriais, não certificação automática CEFR.
humanReviewChecklist: Revisar compreensão e naturalidade do inglês no nível indicado.
Revisar se cada pergunta tem exatamente uma resposta apoiada no texto.
Revisar continuidade, motivação, tom e ambos os finais.
Revisar o registro de autoria e autorização do texto; preencher créditos e evidências das mídias que forem produzidas.
Produzir e escutar WAVs a partir de audioText; revisar e produzir as imagens-base e loops.
Importar como rascunho, validar mídia no servidor e publicar somente após revisão.
